source_refs.note: Nociceptors: a main subheading of 15.6.3 Receptors of Pain & Touch, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 45-45.

blocks.text: Nociceptors detect pain. Pain is defined as a stimulus that causes or is about to cause tissue damage. Nociceptors consist of free nerve endings located throughout the body, especially near surfaces. Different nociceptors may respond to extremes in temperature, very intense pressure, or specific chemicals (including some that are released by injured cells).

blocks.title: For Information
blocks.text:
Thermoreceptors: are naked dendrite endings of sensory neurons. They detect fall and rise in temperature. Cold receptors are located immediately below the epidermis, while warm receptors are located slightly deeper, in the dermis.
Thermoreceptors are also found within the hypothalamus of the brain, where they detect the temperature of the blood and thus monitor the body’s internal (core) temperature.
